questions.question: Which Constitutional Amendment Act has replaced the collegium system of appointing judges to the Supreme Court and High Courts?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the __**99th Amendment Act**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• 99th Constitutional Amendment Act

 
 
• It **formed a National Judicial Appointments Commission.**
 
• 16 State assemblies out of 29 States including Goa, Rajasthan, Tripura, Gujarat and Telangana ratified the Central Legislation, enabling the President of India to give assent to the bill.
 
• In 2015, the Constitution Bench (4:1 Majority) of the Supreme Court declared the 99th Constitutional Amendment and National Judicial Commission (NJAC) unconstitutional on the ground that it violates the Basic Structure of the Constitution of India.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **65th Amendment Act** 

 
 
• The **65th Amendment Act of the Indian Constitution** (1990) is significant as it strengthened the role and functioning of the **National Commission for Scheduled Castes (SCs) and Scheduled Tribes (STs)**.
 
• It replaced the existing multi-member body for SCs and STs with a **National Commission for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes,** under Article 338.
 
• This Commission was given a **constitutional status, **elevating its authority and independence
 
• The Commission was empowered to function as a** quasi-judicial body,** with powers similar to a civil court in certain matters.
 
 
 
• **82nd Amendment Act**
 
 
• **​**The **82nd Amendment Act of the Indian Constitution** (2000) introduced a crucial provision to protect the interests of the Scheduled Castes (SCs) and Scheduled Tribes (STs) in matters of employment. 
 
• The amendment added a **proviso to Article 335 of the Constitution**.
 
• **Article 335 originally states that the claims of SCs and STs** must be taken into consideration in appointments to services and posts, while ensuring the maintenance of efficiency in administration.
 
• The **amendment allowed the government to relax qualifying marks and standards of evaluation for SCs and STs i**n matters of reservation in promotions.
 
 
 
• **52nd Amendment Act**
 
 
• The **52nd Amendment Act of the Indian Constitution** (1985) is a landmark legislation known for introducing the **anti-defection law**.
 
• The amendment added the **Tenth Schedule to the Constitution,** commonly referred to as the Anti-Defection Law.
 
• It **aims to curb political defections by members of the legislature**, which were seen as undermining the stability of governments and the principles of democracy.** **

questions.question: Who led the English Forces in the Battle of Buxar?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Hector Munro__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The English Army in the Battle of Buxar was led by Hector Munro.
 
• The **battle was fought between the East India Company and the combined armies of Mir Qasim, Nawab of Bengal,** the Nawab of Awadh, and the Mughal Emperor Shah Alam II on 22nd October 1764 in Buxar, a small town in Bihar.
 
• The **battle was a decisive victory for the British East India Company**.
 
• The war was put to an **end by the Treaty of Allahabad in the year 1765. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Henry Lawrence (1806–1857)**

 
 
• A British military officer and administrator, Lawrence was one of the key figures in the governance of British India.
 
• He is best remembered for his role during the **Indian Rebellion of 1857**, particularly in the defense of **Lucknow**.
 
• Lawrence was the Chief Commissioner of Oudh (Awadh) and was stationed in Lucknow during the uprising.
 
• He **fortified the British Residency in Lucknow **and led the early stages of its defense. Unfortunately, he was mortally wounded during the siege.
 
• He was part of the famous Lawrence brothers, who were influential in British India.
 
 
 
• **John Nicholson (1821–1857)**
 
 
• A British Army officer, Nicholson played a significant role in the suppression of the **Indian Rebellion of 1857**.
 
• He is known for his leadership during the **Siege of Delhi**, where he led British and Indian troops in retaking the city from rebel forces.
 
• He was **mortally wounded during the assault on Delhi and died shortly after its recapture.**
 
 
 
• **Sir Hugh Wheeler (1789–1857)**
 
 
• A British general who commanded the garrison at **Cawnpore (Kanpur)** during the **Indian Rebellion of 1857**.
 
• Wheeler's role is controversial due to his underestimation of the rebellion's scale and his misplaced trust in the rebel leader **Nana Sahib**.

• The **Ahaia Winter Festival** is primarily organized by the North-Eastern state of **Meghalaya** to promote tourism.
 
• It provides a platform to showcase the vibrant traditions, music, art, and craftsmanship of Meghalaya, particularly **those of the Garo, Khasi, and Jaintia tribes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• The Asian Para Games were established after the **Far East and South Pacific Games for the Disabled (FESPIC Games) ended in 2006.**

questions.question: Freedom of Conscience provided in Article 25 of the Constitution of India is strengthened by which of the following two articles?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Articles 27 and 28**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 27 guarantees freedom from taxation for religious purposes, **stating that no person shall be compelled to pay taxes for the promotion or maintenance of any religion or religious activity.
 
• **Article 28 ensures that no religious instruction** is provided in any educational institution that is wholly funded by the state.
 
• These provisions strengthen the freedom of conscience and religious freedom under Article 25
 
• It **guarantees the right to freely profess, practice, and propagate religion.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 24: **

 
 
• **​**This **article deals with the prohibition of child labour**.
 
• It states **that no child below the age of 14 years shall be employed to work in any factory** or mine or engaged in any other hazardous employment.
 
• While important for protecting children's rights, it does not directly relate to freedom of conscience or religious freedoms.
 
 
 
• **Article 26: **
 
 
• **​**This **article provides the freedom to manage religious affairs. **
 
• It **allows every religious denomination or any section thereof the right **to establish and maintain institutions for religious and charitable purposes, manage its own affairs in matters of religion, and own and acquire property.
 
• This article** strengthens religious freedom and conscience by ensuring religious groups can function independently.**
 
 
 
• **Article 29:**
 
 
• This article ensures the protection of **the cultural and educational rights of minorities.**
 
• It **states that any section of the citizens residing in India **with a distinct language, script, or culture has the right to conserve the same.
 
• It **also guarantees the right to establish and administer educational institutions,** which helps protect the identity and religious beliefs of minority groups.

The correct answer is__** 22**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Constitution of India is the longest-written constitution** of any sovereign nation in the world.
 
• The** original text of the Constitution contained 395 articles in 22 parts and 8 schedules.**
 
• It **came into effect on January 26, 1950**, the day that India celebrates each year as Republic Day.
 
• The number of articles has since increased to 448 due to 105 amendments. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Important Facts about India Constitution​**

 
 
• It was **adopted on November 26, 1949, **and came into effect on January 26, 1950.
 
• It **draws influences from various constitutions like those of the UK, USA, Ireland, and Australia.**
 
• Dr. B.R. Ambedkar is considered the principal architect of the Constitution.
 
• The Constitution is the **supreme law of India**; any law inconsistent with it is void.
 
• **India has a federal structure with a unitary bias**, giving more power to the central government.
 
• It declares India a secular state, ensuring equality for all religions.
 
• The** Constitution can be amended through a detailed process under Article 368.**
 
• It guarantees Fundamental Rights to citizens and lists Fundamental Duties.
 
• The Preamble declares India as a Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, Democratic Republic.

questions.question: What are the most common type of earthquakes?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Tectonic earthquakes **__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Tectonic earthquakes​

 
 
• They are the** most common earthquakes found all over the world.**
 
• These are generated due to the sliding of rocks along a fault plane.
 
• It is caused by the movement of plates when energy accumulated within plate boundary zones is released.
 
• Tectonic earthquakes are usually larger than volcanic earthquakes.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Volcanic earthquakes

 
 
• A special class of tectonic earthquakes is sometimes recognized as a volcanic earthquake. However, these are confined to areas of active volcanoes.
 
• Volcanic earthquakes have different characteristics from the deep and tectonic seismic events that occur along great faults.
 
• They are considerably less devastating and may continue at a detectable level for weeks or months before the eruption.
 
• It is caused by the sudden opening of channels in crustal rocks, rapid changes of motion of magma, excessive accumulation of gas pressure in the crust, roof collapses of subterranean channels emptied of magma.
 
 
 
• **Seismic Earthquakes**
 
 
• Seismic earthquakes **are caused by the sudden release of energy due to tectonic movements**, such as faults or volcanic activity.
 
• The energy release is measured in** terms of magnitude (size) and intensity (impact**), with stronger quakes causing more damage.
 
• They occur frequently along tectonic plate boundaries, **such as the Pacific Ring of Fire.**
 
 
 
• **Reservoir Earthquakes​**
 
 
• These **earthquakes are caused by the filling of large reservoirs, which changes the stress on the Earth's crust.**
 
• They usually occur near the reservoir or dam, with magnitudes typically lower than seismic earthquakes.
 
• The weight and pressure of the water can cause the rupture of faults, **leading to minor earthquakes.**

• The scheme aims to address the challenges that limit the productivity of rice-based cropping systems in these states.

questions.question: India announced the NEP in 1991. NEP stands for _________ .
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**New Economic Policy**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **NEP stands for New Economic Policy**.
 
• India **announced the NEP in 1991 as a series of economic reforms **to improve the country's competitiveness and macroeconomic stability.
 
• The policy was **introduced by Prime Minister P.V. Narasimha Rao** and l**aunched by Finance Minister Dr. Manmohan Singh.**
 
• The **NEP's policies were divided into two groups**: stabilization measures and structural reform measures.
 
• Stabilization **measures were short-term measures to control inflation and correct balance of payments weaknesses.**
 
• Structural reform measures** were long-term measures to improve the economy's efficiency and international competitiveness. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Key Features of the New Economic Policy (1991):
 
• Liberalization:
 
 
• Reduction of Government Control: The NEP reduced the control of the government over various economic activities, leading to the dismantling of the License Raj.
 
• Deregulation: Industries were freed from strict controls and regulations, allowing for easier entry and operation of businesses.
 
 
 
• Privatization:
 
 
• Disinvestment of Public Sector Enterprises: The government started reducing its stake in public sector enterprises (PSEs) to improve efficiency and attract private investment.
 
• Encouragement of Private Sector: Greater role for the private sector in the economy, with less interference from the state.
 
 
 
• Globalization:
 
 
• Opening up to Global Markets: The policy encouraged foreign direct investment (FDI) and allowed foreign companies to operate in India.
 
• Integration with the Global Economy: Reduction in tariffs, quotas, and trade restrictions to make India more competitive globally.
 
 
 
• Financial Sector Reforms:
 
 
• Banking Reforms: Liberalization of interest rates, increased competition among banks, and strengthening of the regulatory framework.
 
• Capital Market Reforms: Modernization of stock markets, establishment of SEBI (Securities and Exchange Board of India) to regulate the securities market.
 
 
 
• Tax Reforms:
 
 
• Rationalization of Tax Structure: Introduction of reforms to simplify the tax system and improve compliance.
 
 
 
• Objectives of NEP (1991):
 
 
• Boost Economic Growth: By opening up the economy, the NEP aimed to increase productivity and efficiency in various sectors.
 
• Reduce Fiscal Deficit: Addressing the fiscal crisis by reducing government expenditure and increasing revenue.
 
• Improve Balance of Payments: Encourage exports and attract foreign investment to improve the balance of payments situation.
 
 
 
• Impact of NEP (1991):
 
 
• Economic Growth: The NEP led to significant economic growth in India, with higher GDP growth rates in the years following the reforms.
 
• Increased Foreign Investment: The reforms attracted substantial foreign investment into the country.
 
• Expansion of Private Sector: The private sector grew rapidly, contributing to job creation and industrial growth.
 
• Improvement in Infrastructure: Reforms led to better infrastructure development, including telecommunications, power, and transportation.

questions.question: Gross national product is the total market value of all final goods and services produced by _________.

options.text: nationals and NRIs of a country during a period of five years
Country’s residents over a period of time
national and foreigners during a period of two years
nationals of a country during a period of five year

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Country’s residents over a period of time**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• GNP - Gross National Product

 
 
• It is the **total value of all the final products and services in a given period in terms** of production by a country's residents.
 
• It is **considered an important economic indicator by economists.**
 
• It is used for finding solutions to economic issues such as poverty and inflation.
 
• It is **Country’s residents over a period of time**
 
• The basic distinction between GDP and GNP is the difference in estimating the production output by foreigners in a country and by nationals outside of a country.
 
 
 
• Gross National Product includes government expenditure, personal consumption expenditure, private domestic investments, net exports, and income earned by nationals overseas, and eliminates the income of foreign residents within the domestic economy. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** Other concepts related to it

 
• Gross Domestic Product

 
 
• It is the value of all final goods and services produced by the normal residents as well as non-residents in the domestic territory of the country but does not include Net Factor Income from Abroad.
 
• The important point to remember is whatever is produced in India, whether by an Indian or foreign national is part of Indian GDP.
 
 
 
• Net National Product
 
 
• In the production of GNP of a year, **a country uses some fixed assets or capital goods like Machinery, Equipment, and technology, etc.**
 
• The capital goods like machinery, building, and equipment undergo regular wear and tear during the production process, which reduces their value. This fall in the value of capital assets due to regular wear and tear is called depreciation.
 
• When the **Depreciation is deducted from the Gross National Product, then we get Net National Product**.

questions.question: Which of the following parts/structures is located at the topmost part of a Stupa?

questions.question: Who among the following introduced binominal nomenclature of biological classification?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Linnaeus**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Carolus Linnaeus **introduced binomial nomenclature, the modern system of naming organisms, in the 1750s.
 
• Linnaeus is** also known as the "father of modern taxonomy"**
 
• Linnaeus was a **Swedish biologist and physician **who was born in Råshult, Sweden in 1707.
 
• Linnaeus **classified organisms into two kingdoms: Plantae and Animalia.**
 
• He **used a variety of criteria for classification, including cell wall, locomotion, mode of nutrition, and response to external stimuli.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Aristotle****​**

 
 
• Aristotle is often considered the **father of biology** due to his extensive work in **natural history** and his systematic study of living organisms.
 
• He made detailed observations of plants and animals, classifying them into **two broad groups**: **animals** and **plants**.
 
• He also introduced the concept of **empirical observation** and **classification** of species based on their characteristics.
 
• **Aristotle's classification system** was based on physical traits and behaviour.
 
• He proposed a **ladder of life** where organisms were organized from simpler forms to more complex ones.
 
• His works laid the foundation for **taxonomy** and **ecology**, though many of his ideas were later revised or replaced by more modern scientific theories.
 
 
 
• **John Ray**
 
 
• **​**John Ray was an English naturalist who is considered one of the **founders of modern biology and taxonomy.**
 
• Ray’s work was instrumental in the development of the **scientific classification of plants and animals.**
 
• He made a distinction between **species and varieties** and recognized the importance of r**eproductive isolation in maintaining species.**
 
• In his landmark work, Historia Plantarum (1686), Ray classified plants into **families and genera, and established a foundation for later plant classification systems.**
 
• He was also one of the first to define the concept of species as a group of organisms capable of interbreeding and producing fertile offspring.​
 
 
 
• **Charles Darwin **
 
 
• **​**Charles Darwin is** best known for his groundbreaking work on the theory of evolution**.
 
• His theory posited that species evolve over time through the process of natural selection, where traits that are advantageous for survival are more likely to be passed on to future generations.
 
• His **seminal book, On the Origin of Species (1859),** proposed that all species of life have descended from common ancestors and that the process of natural selection drives the diversity of life.
 
• Darwin’s work fundamentally changed the way scientists understood the origin of species and their adaptation to the environment.
 
• His **ideas laid the foundation for modern evolutionary biology and helped explain the diversity of life on Earth.**
 
• Darwin’s theory also influenced various fields, including g**enetics, paleontology, and ethology (study of animal behavior).**​

questions.question: A solution contains 50 g of sugar in 450 g of water. Calculate the concentration in terms of mass by mass percentage of the solution.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**10%**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• To **calculate the mass by mass percentage of the solution**,

 
 
• we **need to divide the mass of sugar by the total mass of the solution (sugar + water) and then multiply by 100%.**
 
• **Total mass of the solution:** 50 g (sugar) + 450 g (water) = 500 g
 
• **Mass by mass percentage:** (50 g sugar / 500 g solution) * 100% = 10%
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mass percentage** is a way to express the concentration of a component (like a solute) in a mixture (like a solution).
 
• It tells you how many grams of that component are present in 100 grams of the total mixture.
 
• **Calculation of Mass percentage**
 
 
• **​**Mass percentage = (Mass of component / Total mass of mixture) * 100%

questions.question: Which special symbol is commonly used by geologists to describe the orientation of rock beds, faults, fractures, cuestas, igneous dikes and sills?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Strike and Dip**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Geologists commonly **use "strike and dip" to describe the orientation of rock beds, faults, fractures, cuestas, igneous dikes, and sills**.
 
• **Strike** 
 
 
• **It refers to the direction of the horizontal line** formed by the intersection of a rock layer and a horizontal plane
 
• It is **typically expressed in degrees, using a compass direction** (e.g., North-South, East-West).
 
• It represents the direction of the trend of the bedding planes (i.e., the rock layer's horizontal orientation
 
 
 
• **Dip** 
 
 
• It i**ndicates the angle at which the rock layer is inclined relative to the horizontal plane.**
 
• It is expressed as an angle,** with the dip direction being the direction in which the rock layer is tilted downward.**
 
• Dip is always **measured perpendicular** to the strike.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Scale Indicator**

 
 
• A **scale indicator is a symbol used on maps, charts, and diagrams to represent the scale of the map.**
 
• It **indicates the relationship between a distance on the map** and the actual distance in the real world.
 
• **For example**, a scale might show that 1 cm on the map equals 100 meters in reality.
 
 
 
• **Average Directional Index (ADX)**
 
 
• **​**The Average Directional Index (ADX) is a statistical tool used in **technical analysis** in finance and trading.
 
• It is used to measure the strength of a trend in the market (whether the trend is strong or weak)
 
 
 
• **Compass Rose**
 
 
• **​**A **compass rose is a diagram showing directions **(North, South, East, West, and intermediate directions) on a map, chart, or compass.
 
• It **provides orientation and helps in navigation.**

questions.question: The phenomenon of liquidity trap is based upon which of the following aspects of demand for money?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Speculative**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phenomenon of liquidity trap is **based on the speculative aspect of demand for mone**y
 
• A liquidity trap is an economic situation where people hoard financial capital instead of investing or consuming it as the interest rates are low and savings rates are high which renders the monetary policy ineffective.
 
• Speculative demand for money is inversely related to the rate of interest i.e. higher the rate of interest smaller will be speculative demand for money and vice versa. 
 
• Therefore curve of speculative demand for money is downward sloping to right.
 
• A liquidity trap is caused when people hoard cash because they expect an adverse event such as deflation, insufficient aggregate demand, or war.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Transaction demand**

 
 
• Transaction demand is the **amount of money people and companies need for their daily transactions**.
 
• It's a **determinant of the demand for money, along with asset demand and precautionary demand. **
 
• In a healthy economy, t**ransaction demand is high because people want more goods and services.**
 
• **Example**
 
 
• **​**Carrying cash to buy groceries, utensils, or a train ticket is an example of transaction demand. 
 
 
 
 
 
• **Precautionary Demand**
 
 
• The precautionary demand **for money is the act of holding real balances of money for use in a contingency**.
 
• As receipts and payments cannot be perfectly foreseen, **people hold precautionary balances to minimize the potential loss arising from a contingency.**
 
• **Example**
 
 
• **​**Saving for emergencies: A family may increase their savings during a recession to cover unexpected expenses like job loss or medical emergencies. 
 
 
 
 
 
• **Velocity of circulation**
 
 
• **​**If the **velocity of money is increasing, then the velocity of circulation is an indicator that transactions between individuals are occurring more frequently.**
 
• A higher velocity is a sign that the same amount of money is being used for a number of transactions.
 
• A **high velocity indicates a high degree of inflation**

questions.question: The process of removing government-imposed limits or impediments is known as:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Liberalisation**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The process of removing government-imposed limits or** impediments is known as liberalizatio**n
 
• **Liberalization is the process of removing government-imposed barriers or restrictions.**
 
• This can occur **when something that was previously prohibited is no longer prohibited, or when government regulations are reduced**
 
• **Example**
 
 
• **​**In 1991, India lifted restrictions and opened up its economy for foreign investors.
 
• This was part of the LPG Reforms, **which had three pillars: liberalization, privatization, and globalization. **
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Privatization:

 
 
• It is the increment of the dominating role of private sector companies and the reduced role of public sector companies.
 
• In other words, it is the reduction of ownership of the management of a government-owned enterprise.
 
• Government companies can be converted into private companies in two ways:
 
 
• By disinvestment
 
• By withdrawal of governmental ownership and management of public sector companies.
 
 
 
 
 
• Globalization:
 
 
• It means integrating the economy of one country with the global economy.
 
• During Globalization the main focus is on foreign trade & private and institutional foreign investment. 
 
• The main aim of Globalization is to transform the world towards independence and integration of the world as a whole by setting various strategic policies.
 
• Globalization is attempting to create a borderless world, wherein the need of one country can be driven from across the globe and turn into one large economy.
